posts.text:
Sunday, Nov 1: Toronto's streetcars lost 698 hours to delays, across all routes.

Hardest hit: 501 Queen westbound, where the typical trip lost 27 min.
Smoothest: 507 Long Branch westbound, 10 min.

https://freems88.github.io/ttc-streetcar-delays/

Sunday's slowest spot: Northbound on Dundas St West, approaching Bloor St West.
The average streetcar lost 2 min 17 s here. Across 229 trips, that adds up to 8.7 hours.
This signal has transit priority.
posts.alt: 3D map of Dundas St West around Bloor St West, rotated to Toronto's street grid. Delay is drawn as a coloured ridge above the track, rising where streetcars lose time; the northbound stretch at Bloor St West is highlighted, peaking at about 2 min 17 s lost per streetcar.

posts.text:
Sunday, Nov 1: on frequent routes, bunching and missing cars made the average wait at a stop 1.6 min longer than scheduled.

Worst: 510 Spadina northbound, 3.4 min extra; 1 in 3 cars bunched.
Steadiest: 511 Bathurst southbound, 0.5 min extra.

https://freems88.github.io/ttc-streetcar-delays/#v=wait

Sunday, Nov 1: at the busiest moment (5:00 pm), 136 streetcars were in service, against 140 scheduled.
Overall, 98% of scheduled streetcar service ran, and buses ran 764 hours on streetcar routes.
Furthest behind: 509 Harbourfront, at 86% of its scheduled service.

Service changes, Sunday, Nov 1:
• 501 Queen, partly by bus: Long Branch Loop Streetcar Track Renewal Work
• 504 King, partly by bus: Temporary service change due to City of Toronto work
